case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread concerns Bluetooth qualification planning for a new product that was initially expected to follow a Controller Subsystem-style qualification approach using RF and RF PHY testing combined with an existing controller component qualification. During a pre-registration review using the post-July-2024 Bluetooth SIG qualification system, qualification feasibility issues were identified before testing began. The discussion focused on power class consistency, Inter-Layer Dependency validation, qualification architecture, and the impact of the new Qualification Workspace consistency checks. The consultant recommended reconsidering the planned registration structure to reduce qualification risk and improve the likelihood of successful product listing.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The consultant analyzed the proposed combination of RF/RF PHY test evidence with an existing controller component qualification and found an Inter-Layer Dependency conflict between RF PHY Class 1 support requirements and the referenced controller stack's LL ICS settings. The thread explains that changing the LL declaration to avoid the conflict would trigger extensive new testing obligations under current TCRL requirements, including BB-related testing. The consultant also highlighted that qualification paths previously accepted under Launch Studio are now subject to additional Consistency Check validation in Qualification Workspace. As a result, creating an intermediate Controller Subsystem-equivalent registration could provide limited value because downstream product registration compatibility cannot be fully predicted in advance.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's reasoning is driven by qualification-system consistency rules rather than test execution alone. A referenced controller qualification must remain logically compatible with the RF PHY capabilities declared by the new design. If resolving the dependency conflict requires modifying inherited controller behavior, substantial additional qualification testing may be triggered. Because new Qualification Workspace consistency checks evaluate combinations that were previously unchecked, the safest approach is to avoid creating an intermediate qualification layer whose later usability cannot be guaranteed and instead perform product registration directly using the RF/RF PHY evidence together with compatible referenced qualifications.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Selecting an incompatible controller qualification or forcing ICS changes could create invalid qualification dependencies, trigger extensive additional testing requirements, and jeopardize successful registration. Creating an intermediate Controller Subsystem-equivalent registration without confirming downstream compatibility could result in qualification work that later provides little or no practical value during product listing. Misalignment between power class declarations and referenced qualification assets could also prevent successful registration completion.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Before committing to Bluetooth testing and qualification strategy, perform a Qualification Workspace feasibility review using the exact referenced QDIDs, ICS declarations, power-class assumptions, and intended registration architecture. Post-2024 consistency checks can invalidate qualification paths that previously appeared acceptable, so registration design should be validated before investing in testing or intermediate qualification layers.
